hypotheses.justification: The proof never uses `W.IsElliptic`. The conclusion `W.IsTwoKernel (X - C (Q.coordsOrZero).1)` is a structure over a general `CommRing`, so it needs no ellipticity. `W.toAffine.Point` and its `AddCommGroup` instance (Mathlib `Affine/Point.lean`, line 805, in the section with only `[Field F] [DecidableEq F]`) do not need it either. `addOrderOf Q` therefore elaborates without it. The only external lemma in the proof, `WeierstrassCurve.eval_Psi2Sq_of_two_nsmul_eq_zero`, has signature `{F} [Field F] [DecidableEq F] {W : Affine F} {x y} (h : W.Nonsingular x y) (h2 : 2 • some x y h = 0)`, with no `IsElliptic`. The nonsingularity hypothesis comes from the point `Q = some x y hxy` itself. The remaining steps (`natDegree_X_sub_C`, `coeff` computations, `addOrderOf_zero`, `addOrderOf_nsmul_eq_zero`) are purely algebraic. So deleting the binder leaves the theorem true, and the same proof compiles.
